description: 完整交叉 resident 形成文化与 newcomer 适应伙伴日程
research_question: 陌生主体恢复共同符号的速度和最终结构，是否由 resident 形成时的角色对称性决定，还是取决于适应阶段的伙伴覆盖？

factorial.resident_cultures: static/random role order × fixed A, rotating A/B, random A/B/C formation

social_learning.newcomer: identity 0 communication modules freshly reset; visual frontend inherited from the same visual group
social_learning.trainable: newcomer sender and receiver communication modules only
social_learning.residents: communication and private visual modules frozen
social_learning.role_mode: same role mode as resident culture

measures.interpretation: Schedule effects are social-learning effects only when resident culture and visual group are held fixed; all results remain finite-protocol evidence.

hypotheses: For a fixed resident culture, broader adaptation partner coverage should improve recovery and reduce dependence on one partner schedule.
Random-role resident cultures should retain lower role spread under every adaptation schedule.
Resident role randomization and adaptation schedule coverage may interact: a symmetric culture should need less partner coverage to recover.
controls_and_limits: Resident culture and adaptation schedule are fully crossed; all other training and evaluation budgets are held fixed.
Newcomer shares a frozen visual frontend family with residents; perception learning is deferred.
The task remains the finite six-site, three-resource, two-token grounded protocol inherited from v0.43.
All chains use centralized shared reward and no asynchronous or symbolic demonstration channel.
